doc.title: Derek Brown interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 5, 2021

title: The fifty-state, fifty-gig RV tour
summary: Brown explains the nine-month RV tour with his wife and what he learned about America's landscapes.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Congratulations on your, was it last year you did a fifty state tour?
Yeah. Like a year and a half ago. Fifty gigs, fifty states. We made it all. Nine months in an RV.
You couldn’t think of anything challenging to do, hey?

No, no. And my wife and I, she got to come with — and we both love to travel. And usually I’m doing gigs by myself like flying here or there. I’ve been to Europe a lot of times. And a lot of times she doesn’t get to come with me. And so we were trying to think of you know what? I should do more stuff in the U.S. and maybe I could string them all together. And when we started putting feelers out for if something could work we were getting a really good response from all over the country. And we were like I wonder if we just go a step further and why don’t we just try to get all the states. You know? Why not? Make it a nice theme, like fifty states, fifty gigs.
Well this isn’t really a musical question but did you learn anything about America?

Uh let’s see, yeah, I’m sure I did. I mean I learned, I mean it’s an extremely beautiful country, such a variety of landscapes, even people. But you know we often think of, when you want to go on a vacation, well some people do, like you’ve got to go to other countries, you’ve got to go to Europe. But man we have it all here. People often ask me like what my favorite states were and I have to kind of go along with the cliché that yes, Hawaii and Alaska were pretty amazing, because they’re both so exotic. But you know there was so much beauty. And we were in the fall in the Northeast, so around like the Finger Lakes and we did the Adirondacks right around, right when it was beautiful colors. And my wife was really good about kind of almost forcing me, I have to say that, forcing me to have — to not schedule a gig every day so that we could have a trip to Acadia National Park or you know, to see the Grand Canyon. So I’m actually quite grateful for that. So instead of my memories of the great United States just being oh yeah © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-
I saw a lot of cool concert halls. It was like no I saw these amazing forests and these valleys and the oceans. You know so it was quite an experience all around.
